snapshot.title: UPSC Schemes 1: Social Sector & Welfare
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ UPSC v12.0 Hook: 5 Lakh: PMJAY. 6000: KISAN. Rural Dev: MGNREGS. Women: Shakti. Housing: PMAY.

quick_notes.title: MGNREGS
quick_notes.detail: Min Rural Dev. 100 days work. Legal right. Social audit mandatory. Geo-MGNREGA for tracking.
quick_notes.explanation: MGNREGS stands for Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, which is a government program under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). This scheme is run by the Ministry of Rural Development and guarantees every rural household a legal right to get up to 100 days of paid work in a year. A legal right means that if the government does not provide work within 15 days of you asking, you are entitled to an unemployment allowance. Social audit is a mandatory process where local villagers publicly examine

quick_notes.title: Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY)
quick_notes.detail: Min Health. ₹5 Lakh/family/year. Secondary/Tertiary care. Paperless/Cashless. World's largest.
quick_notes.explanation: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, or PM-JAY for short, is a health insurance scheme run by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, which is the government department responsible for health matters. Under this scheme, each eligible family gets health insurance coverage of up to 5 lakh rupees per family per year, meaning the government will pay for medical treatment costs up to that amount for the whole family in one year. The scheme covers secondary care, which is treatment by specialists like a cardiologist or orthopedist, and tertiary care, which is advanced hospital care such as surgeries or cancer treatment. Patients do not need to fill any paper forms or pay any money at the hospital because the scheme is paperless and cashless, so the hospital directly bills the government. PM-JAY is the world's largest health insurance scheme, providing free hospital treatment to over 500 million poor and vulnerable people in India.

quick_notes.title: PM-KISAN
quick_notes.detail: Min Agri. ₹6,000/year in 3 installments. Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). All landholding farmers eligible.
quick_notes.explanation: PM-KISAN stands for Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi, which is a scheme of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. Under this scheme, eligible farmers receive a total of 6,000 rupees every year, paid in three equal installments of 2,000 rupees each. The money is sent directly to the farmer's bank account through a system called Direct Benefit Transfer, or DBT, which means no middlemen are involved. The scheme is available to all farmers who own land, meaning they have legal documents showing they are the landowners.

quick_notes.title: PMAY (U+G)
quick_notes.detail: Housing for All. PMAY-G (Min Rural Dev). PMAY-U (Min Housing & Urban Affairs).
quick_notes.explanation: PMAY stands for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, which is a government scheme to provide housing for all people in India. PMAY is divided into two parts: PMAY-G (Gramin, meaning rural) and PMAY-U (Urban). PMAY-G is run by the Ministry of Rural Development and gives financial help to build or improve houses in villages. PMAY-U is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and gives similar help for houses in cities and towns. Both schemes aim to ensure that every family has a pucca house with basic facilities like water, electricity, and a toilet.

quick_notes.title: Nutrition Schemes
quick_notes.detail: POSHAN Abhiyaan. PM-POSHAN (Mid-day meal). Mission Shakti (Women safety/empowerment).
quick_notes.explanation: The POSHAN Abhiyaan, which stands for Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment, is a government program focused on improving the nutritional status of children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers. PM-POSHAN, short for Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman and formerly called the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, provides a free hot cooked meal to schoolchildren in classes 1 to 8 to boost their nutrition and encourage school attendance. Mission Shakti is a government initiative aimed at the safety, security, and empowerment of women, combining efforts like helplines, one-stop crisis centers, and awareness programs. All three schemes work together to address malnutrition and support vulnerable groups in India.
